title: Load balancing, and why you need N+1

steps.caption: One server that handles 1k rps, at 600 rps. Utilization ρ = 0.6: fine.
1.5k rps. The server can only do 1k: the queue fills, requests time out, and client retries add even more load.
Put a load balancer in front of three servers. Each gets a third: 500 rps, ρ 0.5.
One server dies. Health checks take it out of rotation: the other two get 750 rps each and nobody notices.
Now traffic grows to 2.4k rps with one server still down. Two servers can't do it. Size for N+1: enough capacity with your biggest piece missing.
